title: Oral-history exhibition and language corpus

threads.title: Harbor Voices listening exhibition
threads.scope: Curate, license, install and assess a listening exhibition using the fictional Harbor Voices oral-history collection.

threads.title: Harbor Voices vowel corpus
threads.scope: Create an independently commissioned annotated vowel corpus from selected Harbor Voices recordings for a language research group.

threads.title: Camping stove repair
threads.scope: Repair and test a camping stove with a loose pot support.

captures.text: Harbor Voices exhibition brief: choose six oral-history clips, obtain listening-room permissions, and install headphones with captions for the winter opening.
captures.rationale: Selection, permissions and installation share one exhibition deliverable.

captures.text: The language group separately commissioned a vowel-annotation corpus from Harbor Voices. Its research files and permissions are independent of the listening exhibition.
captures.rationale: The same source collection supports a distinct research deliverable.

captures.text: Scanned permission form HV-4: exhibit clip at the Harbor Voices listening room; an additional permitted-use field is hidden by a folded page corner.
captures.rationale: The visible text establishes exhibition membership but cannot identify the hidden additional use.

captures.text: Exhibition edit: trim the long pause before the ferry story, but preserve the speaker's final sentence in the listening-room version.
captures.rationale: Clip editing implements the listening exhibition.

captures.text: Camping stove pot support is loose at the hinge. Replace the retaining pin and test stability with an empty pan outdoors.
captures.rationale: A camping-equipment repair is unrelated to the archive deliverables.

captures.text: Unfolded HV-4 permission form: in addition to the listening exhibition, it authorizes this recording's inclusion in the separately commissioned Harbor Voices vowel corpus.
captures.rationale: The complete form explicitly covers both independently scoped uses.

captures.text: Vowel corpus annotation guide: retain untrimmed pause boundaries and mark vowel intervals on the original Harbor Voices audio. Do not annotate the exhibition edit.
captures.rationale: A research-specific method belongs to the independent corpus project.

captures.text: Exhibition caption proof: ferry-story clip, large text, transcript aligned to the final listening-room edit; the opening date remains on the back panel.
captures.rationale: Accessible caption production continues the exhibition.

captures.text: Listening-room installation walkthrough: six headphones play the edited Harbor Voices clips, and the ferry-story caption can be read from the seated position.
Vowel corpus quality check found two interval labels reversed. Correct them in the research annotation file before delivering the corpus to the language group.
captures.rationale: Quality control and delivery preparation are corpus phases.

captures.text: Listening exhibition visitor review: the ferry clip is clear, but the caption's last line catches glare. Tilt that panel and record the adjustment in the exhibition report.
captures.rationale: Visitor findings and installation revision stay in the exhibition project.

captures.text: Vowel corpus delivery manifest: original-audio references, corrected interval labels and permission HV-4 included. The language group accepted the research package.
captures.rationale: Concludes delivery of the independently commissioned corpus.

events.reason: The unfolded form in c06 shows that HV-4 also authorizes the vowel corpus. Keep the exhibition link and explicitly add the corpus link to the folded scan.

events.text: Exhibition edit revised: shorten, rather than remove, the long pause before the ferry story; preserve the speaker's final sentence in the listening-room version.

challenges: A shared recording collection does not establish one undertaking.
A partially legible source can have one supported membership while another remains unknown.
An explicit correction can add a second supported membership without removing the first.
Licensing, accessible captions and visitor review belong with their exhibition.
authorNotes: The oral histories are fictional descriptions without real speakers or personal data. No wholly unresolved capture is required here: the initial folded scan has a positively supported exhibition membership, and only its additional use is unknown.
